Question: Is it illegal for police to sit across my house and watch me and identify cars of people who are parked in my driveway?
Answer: Nope. They can sit on a public street all they want. They can run plates of cars parked in plain view in your driveway all they want. Whether they can do anything with any information they gather is a totally different matter, and you didn’t ask that, so there ya go.

Name: Eileen Wood
Question: Do retired military service members receive a military funeral?
Answer: Absolutely, IF the family wants one. It’s not automatic - you have to request it. When my father died in 1985, he was a 31-year Army veteran. We had a full-on military funeral for him here in Las Vegas, with an honor guard from Fort Irwin, CA. Then we buried him at the National Cemetery at Fort Sam Houston, TX. When my Air Force veteran husband died in 2012, we had him buried in the Southern Nevada Veterans’ Cemetery (we had moved Dad there many, many years earlier). We just had the cemetery provide the honor guard for his funeral. When my Army veterans brother died (2004) and my brother-in-law died (2016) we had private burials. Just the family and the cemetery worker burying the urns. Neither of them wanted a full on military funeral.

Question: My ex-boyfriend wants me to give him all the money back he spent on me during our relationship and if I don't pay him back by November he's taking me to court. Can he do that?
Answer: In the US, anyone can try to sue anyone for anything at any time. Call his bluff and tell him go ahead. I’ll bet dollars to donuts he never does. He’s just trying to f**k with you. Assuming that he DID have the money to pay an attorney to file a case, whether a judge will actually hear it is a different matter. Whether he wins his case is yet another matter. In this case, he’d be lucky to even have a judge agree to hear it. It’d be considered a frivolous lawsuit if he’s just looking for money he spent on things like dinners, movies, etc. If your ex paid for something substantial - like, he paid your way through college solely because you were in a relationship and there was a stated expectation of the relationship lasting, but YOU broke up with him right after graduation - then he MIGHT have a shot at being heard and might even have a shot at winning.

Question: I gave in my 2-week notice period, but I’m still getting shifts on my schedule when the notice period has ended. What do I do?
Answer: Once your 2-week period is up, you are no longer an employee of the company. I would make ONE courtesy call to whomever makes the schedules, just to be sure they got the notice that I will not be an employee on the dates they have scheduled me to work. Then I’d go on my merry way to my new job and let the last one sort things out themselves.
